tweet_summary: Claims (with a stern Trump photo + FIFA logo) that 'MORE THAN 38,700 HOTEL BOOKINGS FOR 2026 FIFA WORLD CUP RESERVATIONS IN THE USA HAVE BEEN CANCELLED,' tied to US-politics boycott sentiment in the replies.
why_note_decision: The precise '38,700 cancelled hotel bookings' figure is a fabricated/unverified statistic with no official source; fact-checking (DW; Grok summary) traces it to social media and notes the closest real figure is ~16,800 withdrawn World Cup ticket applications, plus FIFA's own contractual cancellation of hotel room blocks for unrelated demand reasons. The tweet launders an unverified specific number to ~860k viewers as established fact. A note correcting the fabricated statistic is warranted (I disagree with the provisional no_note_needed: a precise false number presented as fact is exactly the kind of claim a note should address).
judge_guidance: A correct note must establish that the specific '38,700 cancelled hotel bookings' figure is unverified/unsupported by any official source. It should distinguish it from the real, different facts: roughly 16,800 World Cup TICKET applications were reported withdrawn (not hotel bookings), and FIFA separately released/cancelled blocks of hotel rooms for demand reasons - neither equals '38,700 cancelled hotel reservations.' PASS only if the note debunks the precise 38,700 hotel-cancellation number using a reliable source (e.g. DW fact-check) and does not simply validate the boycott narrative. FAIL if it asserts the figure is true, if it conflates ticket withdrawals with hotel cancellations, or if it provides no source.
reference_note: There is no official source for the claim that 38,700 hotel bookings for the 2026 FIFA World Cup were cancelled. Fact-checkers trace the figure to social media; the nearest verified number is roughly 16,800 withdrawn ticket applications (not hotel bookings), and FIFA has denied a mass-cancellation narrative. https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-are-fans-cancelling-world-cup-2026-tickets-over-us-immigration-fears/a-75562821

original_unhelpful_note.text: No evidence confirms over 38,700 cancelled hotel bookings for the 2026 FIFA World Cup; reported figures refer to unverified ticket application withdrawals, which FIFA has denied as fake news. https://www.dw.com/en/fact-check-are-fans-cancelling-world-cup-2026-tickets-over-us-immigration-fears/a-75562821 https://www.marca.com/en/world-cup/2026/01/14/6966d713e2704e0c6a8b4597.html
original_unhelpful_note.failure_reason: Note is substantively correct and well-aimed at a fabricated statistic, but it is in NEEDS_MORE_RATINGS (not a confirmed failure). Its tag spread (OpinionSpeculation 16, NoteNotNeeded 15) suggests raters split on whether the boycott framing made the number 'opinion.' A tighter note nailing the fabricated specific figure should land; it is the reference model here.

fact_check.notes: DW and others find the 38,700 hotel-cancellation figure unverified and social-media-sourced. Real data: ~16,800 ticket applications withdrawn; FIFA itself cancelled hotel room blocks for demand reasons. The tweet conflates/invents a precise number.

importance.lens_rationale: High-reach fabricated statistic shaping a politically charged boycott narrative; correcting invented precise numbers supports epistemic hygiene, though world-stakes are moderate.
